svg.title: KRBTGT PASSWORD RESET ON DOMAIN CONTROLLERS
svg.desc: A management computer (or a domain controller) runs Reset-KrbtgtPassword.ps1. The read-only pre-flight reads the domain, the PDC emulator, every writable DC, the krbtgt account and its unicodePwd replication version, the Kerberos policy from SYSVOL and the replication health. A reset is performed on the PDC emulator, replicated with Sync-ADObject to every writable DC and verified there. The Kerberos clients and services keep working after reset 1 because the password history holds two keys; after reset 2 every ticket issued before reset 1 is rejected. The lower panel shows the two-reset cycle, the compromise mode and the STIG outcome for V-254427 / WN22-DC-000430 and its Server 2025, 2019 and 2016 equivalents.
svg.text: KRBTGT PASSWORD RESET ON DOMAIN CONTROLLERS
DISA STIG V-254427 · WN22-DC-000430 · TWO RESETS PER CYCLE · WAIT >= TICKET LIFETIME · POWERSHELL 7 (5.1 OK) · AD MODULE ONLY
WINDOWS SERVER 2022 STIG V2R11 · 30 SEP 2026 · CAT II
the management computer or a DC runs the script · the PDC emulator takes the reset · every writable DC is verified

g.text: PAW / JUMP HOST OR A DC · RUNS THE SCRIPT
Runs Reset-KrbtgtPassword.ps1 with the ActiveDirectory module over
LDAP; no agent, no download, no other tool
Domain, PDC emulator, writable DCs, RODCs
LDAP bind to every writable DC
Reset 1 of 2 or 2 of 2 (state file + AD version)
STOP if < ticket lifetime since the last reset

text.font-family: Cascadia Mono, Consolas, Courier New, monospace
Cascadia Mono, Consolas, Courier New, monospace

g.text: one JSON record per reset · exit 1 on Open / STOP
IMPORTANT · NO SECRET IS EVER WRITTEN
The new password is 64 random characters from a cryptographic RNG, built as
a read-only SecureString, never shown, logged or hashed.
PS 7 OR 5.1 · RSAT AD · DOMAIN ADMIN · LDAP
TAKES THE RESET · REPLICATES TO ALL WRITABLE DCS
Set-ADAccountPassword -Reset on CN=krbtgt, then Sync-ADObject to
every other writable DC and verification on each one
Verified on the PDC before anything else
Poll every DC until it shows version N+1
Not confirmed = FAIL, next reset refused
After reset 1: old key still accepted (N-1)
After reset 2: the pre-reset key is gone
That is why the STIG wants two resets
The old key cannot be restored. If something breaks, clients recover by
re-authenticating; Microsoft: a reboot is the only reliable recovery.
WRITABLE DCs ONLY · RODC krbtgt_* NOT TOUCHED
EVERY TGT IS SEALED WITH THE KRBTGT KEY
Users, computers and services hold TGTs for up to MaxTicketAge (10 h)
and service tickets for up to MaxServiceAge (600 min)
KDCs accept tickets from key N and N-1
Nobody notices; new TGTs use the new key
Tickets issued before reset 1 are rejected
Both resets in one run, no wait
Every ticket in the domain is invalid at once
Open sessions, until their service ticket renews
TIP · WAIT AT LEAST THE TICKET LIFETIME
The script derives the wait from the Kerberos policy (longest of MaxTicketAge
and MaxServiceAge) and refuses reset 2 before it; -MinHoursBetweenResets

svg.text: MaxTicketAge 10 h · MaxServiceAge 600 min · MaxRenewAge 7 d (Windows defaults)
Windows NT\SecEdit\GptTmpl.inf, or -KerberosPolicyPath · the minimum wait between reset 1 and reset 2 is
management computer → PDC → every writable DC
read back from every DC, not from variables
one reset per run, the wait in between · what each step proves
check: Get-ADUser krbtgt -Property PasswordLastSet · more than 180 days old = Open

g.text: PasswordLastSet age vs 180 days: Open / NotAFinding
Exit 1 when Open: a scheduled task can alert
Resets on the PDC, replicates, verifies every DC
PasswordLastSet is fresh: the item is NotAFinding
State file: step 1 · unicodePwd version N+1
Reset 2 is refused before the wait (STOP: too soon)
Tickets sealed with key N-1 keep working meanwhile
Password history now holds only the two new keys
Golden tickets forged with the old key stop working
State file: step 2 · pair complete · due again in 180 d
Both resets in one run, replication verified between
Every ticket invalid: users and services re-authenticate
Use only when the krbtgt key may be stolen
Run Check weekly (exit 1 = Open) and keep the CSV
Run the pair every 90-180 days, before the due date
